data.title: Fed's Cook says rate hikes needed to lower high inflation
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed's Cook says current policy-rate level not high enough to lower inflation
  • Cook says inflation remains too high and is not easing
  • She was one of two policymakers who dissented in favor of rate hike in October

By Michael S. Derby

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on Friday made a case for more interest rate hikes, saying the US central bank's current policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels she views with "great concern."

"In a different environment, the (Federal Open Market) Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury," given how high inflation is and for how long it has been above the Fed's 2% target, Cook said in the text of a speech to be presented at a central bank conference in Chile.

Cook said the quarter-percentage-point rate hike the Fed delivered at its September 15-16 policy meeting was not enough to moderate current levels of inflation.

What's more, "inflation data received since the September rate increase, including reports last week, fail to provide me with sufficient evidence that inflation is returning to a sustainable path," she said. "There is little evidence inflation is declining."

Cook, who voted for a rate hike at that meeting, was one of two Fed officials who dissented over the Fed's decision last month to leave its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Officials at the October 27-28 meeting signaled that inflation remained too high then even as they refrained from action.

Regarding her dissent in October, Cook said, "My vote reflected the urgency I feel to tackle inflation," which "has been above target for more than five and a half years, and every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward."

RATE HIKE EXPECTED IN DECEMBER

A wide range of Fed officials in recent weeks have signaled support for more rate hikes, and financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise rates at its December 8-9 meeting and to follow that move with more increases next year.

Most Fed officials have made a case for gradual action to lower inflation, arguing that doing so would give the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs. But some, concerned with the most recent inflation data, have speculated that aggressive moves may be needed to bring price pressures to heel.

Cook on Friday said the risk of not acting fast enough to lower inflation could bring more pain later.

"Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve," she said. "If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later to catch up, which could increase stress on our financial system and have unnecessarily damaging effects on American households."

The Fed governor noted that financial conditions remain accommodative and are not providing the needed level of restraint on the economy.

Cook, however, was upbeat on the economy. She said growth is "strong and accelerating" and that the job market remains "solid."

data.title: Tesla proposes $3.1 bln Texas polysilicon plant for solar manufacturing
data.description:
Tesla is planning a $3.1 billion solar-grade polysilicon plant in Texas, according to an application the company filed this week seeking tax incentives for the project.

  • The facility, planned for Nueces County in southern Texas, would create a new domestic source of polysilicon, a material primarly produced by China.

  • "The Project represents a transformative investment in domestic upstream solar manufacturing capacity and in United States critical materials independence," the company said in the application.

  • The plant would begin operations in 2030 and employ 515 workers by 2032, according to the application filed under Texas' Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation program.

  • The application does not specify the value of the requested tax break, though Tesla said the incentive would be an important factor in its site-selection decision.

  • Tesla Chief Executive Elon Musk has a goal to set up 100 gigawatts of US solar manufacturing capacity. Earlier this year, the company revealed it was pursuing a $10.1 billion facility near Houston that would produce solar ingots, wafers and cells.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Moving Sharply Lower As Anthropic Plunges
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Stocks have moved sharply lower over the course of the trading session on Friday, extending the sell-off seen in the previous session. The tech-heavy Nasdaq has shown a particularly steep decline, plunging to its lowest levels in seven months.

Currently, the Nasdaq is just off its lows of the session, down 701.48 points or 2.9 percent at 23,177.72. The S&P 500 is also down 117.04 points or 1.6 percent at 7,058.79, while the narrower Dow is posting a more modest loss, down 73.24 points or 0.2 percent at 49,023.82.

The sell-off on Wall Street comes amid continued weakness among technology stocks, as reflected by the steep drop by the Nasdaq.

A steep drop by shares of Anthropic (ANT) is weigh on the tech sector following its record-breaking initial public offering on Thursday.

Shares of Anthropic are plunging by more than 10 percent after the Claude developer spiked by 17.1 percent on Thursday but ended the day well off its highs of the session.

'The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com.

She added, 'The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run.'

Concerns about the outlook for interest rates may also be contributing to the selling pressure, with at least a quarter point rate hike seen as a near-certainty at the Federal Reserve's monetary policy next month.

Following hawkish comments from several Fed officials, traders have grown increasingly worried the central bank will continue to raise rates in the coming months in order to combat stubborn inflation.

Sector News

Semiconductor stocks are turning in some of the market's worst performances on the day, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeting by 7.9 percent.

Computer hardware and networking stocks are also seeing substantial weakness, dragging the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index and the NYSE Arca Networking Index down by 6.9 percent and 6.3 percent, respectively.

Outside of the tech sector, gold stocks are extending the recent sell-off amid an extended nosedive by the price of the precious metal. Reflecting the weakness in the sector, the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index has plunged by 3.1 percent.

Brokerage, oil service and airline stocks are also seeing considerable weakness, while housing and telecom stocks are bucking the downtrend.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved sharply lower during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index dove by 5.1 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index tumbled by 1.2 percent.

The major European markets have also shown significant moves to the downside. While the German DAX Index is down by 2.3 percent, the French CAC 40 Index is down by 1.6 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index is down by 0.8 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have moved substantially higher amid the extended sell-off on Wall Street. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, is down by 10.2 basis points at 4.950 percent.

data.title: Citi Undercounted $35 Billion in Assets at U.K. Subsidiary — WSJ
data.description:
By Joe Wallace and Gina Heeb

Citigroup underestimated the size of a U.K. subsidiary by $35 billion after mistakes in how it dealt with trades, said people familiar with the matter.

After spotting the problem, the U.S. bank injected extra capital into the subsidiary over the summer, a spokeswoman said in a statement.

The record-keeping blunder is a setback for Chief Executive Jane Fraser's attempt to draw a line under Citi's history of unforced errors. In her almost six years in charge, Fraser has tried to upgrade and streamline Citi's hodgepodge of internal controls and data systems, which landed the bank in the penalty box with regulators.

Citi said it "identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary" this summer. The bank said that even before it responded, the unit's capital never fell below minimum levels required by regulators.

The bank didn't specify how the models misfired. But the mistake related to its calculation of "risk-weighted assets," a banking regulatory measure used to calculate how much capital lenders need to hold aside as a buffer against losses. The riskier the loan or security, the more capital they have to keep.

Reuters earlier reported about Citigroup's shortfall.

The Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency fined Citi $400 million and ordered the bank to fix its risk-management systems in 2020.

That spurred a turnaround program. This May, Fraser told investors that the bank had completed about 90% of the work and that the remainder focused on data governance for regulatory reporting.

"We have better risk-management practices and processes that allow us to assess exposures in real time," she said. "Our monitoring, reporting and stress testing are faster, more dynamic."

But Citi has yet to achieve its goal of persuading the Fed and OCC to remove orders they enforced six years ago, which limit its ability to do deals.

Regulators have spent well over a decade trying to make sure the internal models some big banks use to calculate risk-weighted assets give a fair reflection of their balance sheets. Banks typically strive to hold less capital, because that frees resources to make more loans.

Big international banks such as Citi face capital requirements all over the world as well as in their home market. Investors also follow risk-weighted assets closely when measuring how profitable banks are.

Citi's controls issues are the legacy of a splurge of deals the bank did in the decades before the financial crisis, when the lender wanted to become a financial supermarket. Those acquisitions included purchases in Europe. Citi remains a major player in investment banking and trading in the U.K. and on the Continent.

The bank's broker dealer in London, Citigroup Global Markets Ltd., trades stocks, bonds, commodities and derivatives. It is one of Citi's four main booking hubs globally and recorded $555 billion in total assets at the end of 2025.

The subsidiary's annual report for last year says managers maintain "disciplined oversight of earnings, capital, liquidity and risk-weighted asset efficiency." King Charles awarded Fraser, who was born in Scotland, a damehood for services to the financial sector earlier this year.

The Bank of England, which regulates the broker-dealer subsidiary, declined to comment.

Previous missteps in the U.S. include Citigroup's accidental $900 million payment to creditors of cosmetics company Revlon in 2020.

Citi's problems have landed it in hot water with European regulators as well as their American counterparts. In 2022, a London trader entered a "fat-fingered trade," as it is known in the industry — a sale for $444 billion in stocks instead of $58 million. European markets briefly crashed. U.K. watchdogs fined Citi and faulted the bank for allowing the trader to override a pop-up alert manually.

Write to Joe Wallace at joe.wallace@wsj.com and Gina Heeb at gina.heeb@wsj.com

data.title: US Justice Department drops appeal in Alaska Senate suit
data.description:
By Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff

The US Justice Department dropped its appeal on Thursday in its attempt to block certification of this month's Alaska Senate election after Democratic challenger Mary Peltola secured more than 50% of the vote.

The race was called on Tuesday, two weeks after the election, with the count showing Peltola leading by four percentage points.

  • The Justice Department had sought to preemptively delay certification of the vote in a lawsuit filed before the midterms, so it could probe whether a candidate with a similar name to Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan had led to voter confusion

  • A federal judge had said the government had no such authority

  • In Thursday's filing, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward asked the appeals court to dismiss the case, as the government "reluctantly" acknowledged that there was no viable path to investigate the vote with the ballots already counted and no longer identifiable

  • He also asked the appeals court to vacate the lower court's ruling

  • The closely watched Senate race became the subject of controversy after The New York Times reported days before the vote that Peltola's campaign recruited a retired school teacher named Dan J. Sullivan

  • The government has also launched a criminal probe into whether that recruitment effort was an illegal attempt to confuse voters

  • Peltola has said she had no part in or knowledge of the reported effort

data.title: VistaPrint Partners with Acclaimed Restaurateurs Sohla and Ham El-Waylly for Opening of Brooklyn’s Triangle Bar
data.description:
VistaPrint, the print and design partner to millions of small businesses, today announced a partnership with award-winning chefs and culinary personalities, Sohla and Ham El-Waylly, to support the opening of their newest Brooklyn venture, Triangle Bar. Additional Triangle Bar partners include Anoop Pillarisetti and Michael Tuiach.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120304334/en/

VistaPrint Partners with Acclaimed Restaurateurs Sohla and Ham El-Waylly for Opening of Brooklyn’s Triangle Bar

Located at the base of Fort Greene’s iconic triangular Fowler Square and opening in winter 2026–27, Triangle Bar is reimagining the classic neighborhood bar as a welcoming, all-occasion gathering place. The husband-and-wife duo invite guests to settle in over a pint, enjoy a comforting dinner, or linger over drinks with friends. The bar sits alongside the group’s Brooklyn restaurant, Strange Delight, a critically acclaimed, New Orleans-inspired seafood restaurant and cocktail bar in Fort Greene.

Sohla and Ham partnered with VistaPrint early in the planning process to create a consistent look and feel across every customer-facing touchpoint, including custom-printed sandwich deli paper, signature coasters, menus, takeout packaging and branded signage, t-shirts and hats.

"So much hard work goes into building a small business. Using custom print products is essential when you're trying to build an identity people remember, and we wanted every detail at Triangle Bar to feel intentional,” said Sohla and Ham El-Waylly. “When we opened Strange Delight, coordinating orders across multiple vendors while maintaining quality was exhausting. Having VistaPrint as our one-stop shop for all things branding completely streamlined the process. We're so excited to share Triangle Bar with the Fort Greene community.”

The partnership reflects VistaPrint’s ongoing commitment to championing food and beverage entrepreneurs by providing cohesive, high-quality marketing that turn brands into community destinations from opening day and beyond.

“Sohla and Ham are two of the culinary world’s most trusted voices, embodying the creativity and resilience required to build something completely their own,” said Heather Deschenes, Vice President, North America Marketing at VistaPrint. “Food and beverage branding and marketing live in tangible details that guests interact with every day. By serving as an end-to-end partner for Triangle Bar, VistaPrint makes it easy for entrepreneurs to bring their vision to life.”

For more information about the partnership and to explore the products used for the opening of Triangle Bar, click here.

About VistaPrint

VistaPrint is the print and design partner to millions of small businesses and households around the world. We help small business owners bring their ideas to life through custom print products, easy-to-use digital tools and expert design support. VistaPrint is a Cimpress company ().
